The core innovation lies in representing dynamic scenes using fixed-size sets of 3D Gaussians indexed temporally. Each Gaussian g_{t,k} encodes position, orientation, and scale via μ_{t,k}, q_{t,k}, and s_{t,k}, respectively. The covariance Σ_{t,k} is factored using a unit quaternion q_{t,k} and diagonal scale vector s_{t,k}, enabling efficient rasterization and deformation tracking. This formulation supports retrospective rendering by storing full temporal sequences A = {G_1,...,G_T}. The method avoids explicit temporal coupling mechanisms such as deformation fields or canonical templates, instead relying on geometric evolution alone. In GSE, this translates into a state-space model where each G_t corresponds to a belief state over scene geometry. The standardized dataset framework ensures reproducibility by enforcing synchronized camera setups and deterministic train/validation/test splits. However, the approach may fail under extreme motion blur or occlusion due to limited Gaussian density and fixed cardinality constraints.
